title: Define renormalized Wick powers $:u^3:,:u^2:$ paired with smooth $\psi$ under $\mu$

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (GAP 1).** A correct proof of equivalence $\mu\sim T_\psi^*\mu$ must give rigorous meaning to the renormalized integrals appearing in the candidate density, namely

$$\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} :\!u^3\!:\,\psi\,dx,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} :\!u^2\!:\,\psi^2\,dx,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u\,\psi^3\,dx,$$

as measurable functionals that are finite for $\mu$-a.e. $u$.

**Why nontrivial.** Under $\mu$, samples are distributions of regularity $C^{-1/2-\kappa}$, so $u^2,u^3$ are classically ill-defined. Wick powers are usually defined w.r.t. the Gaussian free field $\nu=N(0,(m^2-\Delta)^{-1})$, but in $d=3$ the $\Phi^4_3$ measure is **singular** w.r.t. $\nu$ (Barashkov–Gubinelli 2021). Therefore the Wick powers and their counterterms must be defined **intrinsically under $\mu$**, e.g. via the regularity-structures lift of the field or the Barashkov–Gubinelli shifted-Gaussian decomposition $u = Z + (\text{drift})$, using exactly the same divergent renormalization constants that enter the construction of $\mu$.

**Deliverable.** (a) State the chosen construction of $\mu$ and its counterterms precisely; (b) define the three functionals above and prove $\mu$-a.s. finiteness; (c) verify the counterterm choice is consistent with the one used to define $\mu$ (no double-counting / mismatched constants).
